name: Two-way sensitivity grid
reader_question: How does a model output change when two drivers vary together, and where does it change sign or magnitude?
relationship: Two-way sensitivity: one model run per cell of a driver-A by driver-B grid, with the base case marked.

capacity.what: values per driver (3 to 7 rows by 3 to 7 columns)

use_when: Two drivers jointly determine a model output and exact cell values matter
The base case must remain visible inside the range of alternatives
avoid_when: More than two drivers need comparison — use tornado
Values are observed rather than model output
A continuous surface is claimed; the grid shows discrete runs only

data_contract.notes: Output measure and unit, labelled as model output
Axis driver and its tested values as display strings
Rows × columns of model output; dimensions must match the axes
Labels of the base-case row and column; must exist in the grid

units: One output unit; shading is a relative ramp over the grid's own minimum and maximum, not an absolute scale.

editable: Native PowerPoint table: values, fills, borders and fonts
not_data_bound: Cell shading is a static fill computed from the fixture; editing a value does not recolour it
The sequential key, base-case marker and model-output tag are positioned shapes and text

table_alternative: The grid is itself a table; a plain unshaded copy serves screen-reader and export use.
variations: Diverging shade around a threshold where sign matters
limitations: Shading is relative to the grid's range, so two grids are not comparable by colour
Shows two drivers only; others are held at base values

excluded_alternatives.reason: Perspective distorts values and hides exact cell outputs
Colour alone cannot carry precise model outputs
